issues.legal_issue: A criminal case should be transferred when the presiding judge’s strongly expressed earlier views create a continuing reasonable apprehension that the judge may not approach the matter fairly, even though the earlier order was set aside and a higher court directed a fresh decision uninfluenced by those views.
material_facts: The complainant sought transfer of a pending criminal sessions case after the trial judge had discharged the accused on the relevant charges.
The discharge order contained strongly worded observations about alleged misuse of the relevant law and concluded that there was no real basis to frame charges under it.
The High Court set aside the discharge order and directed the trial judge to reconsider the matter afresh without being influenced by the earlier observations.
The complainant continued to apprehend that the trial judge’s earlier views would affect the fresh decision.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the criminal case was directed to be transferred to another competent court because the complainant’s apprehension was reasonable despite the safeguards in the remand order.
issues.legal_principle: The majority applied the principle that justice must not only be done but must also appear to be done. Although setting aside an order ordinarily obliterates its findings, and a direction to disregard earlier observations ordinarily safeguards a fresh decision, transfer may still be warranted where the nature and force of those observations create a reasonable apprehension that the judge has committed to an approach and may not take a fair, non-partisan view. The inquiry concerns the reasonableness of the apprehension, not whether the judge is actually biased or incapable of reconsidering the matter. The majority cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion. In dissent, Justice Banumathi considered good and sufficient grounds necessary, treated mere presumptions or casual observations as insufficient, and relied on Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and K.P. Tiwari v. State of M.P.

rule.if: criminal_case_transfer_request and strong_prior_judicial_commitment and remand_neutrality_direction and continuing_reasonable_apprehension

predicates.criminal_case_transfer_request: A party sought transfer of a pending criminal case from the court hearing it.
predicates.strong_prior_judicial_commitment: The presiding judge previously expressed strongly worded views on the matter that must be reconsidered.
predicates.remand_neutrality_direction: A higher court set aside the earlier decision and directed the presiding judge to reconsider the matter without being influenced by the earlier views.
predicates.continuing_reasonable_apprehension: The party continued to have a reasonable apprehension that the earlier views could prevent a fair and non-partisan reconsideration.

issues.definition: When a party seeks transfer of a criminal case, the presiding judge has expressed strongly worded views, a higher court has directed reconsideration without reliance on those views, and a reasonable apprehension of unfair reconsideration nevertheless remains, transfer is required to ensure justice.
